title: Those in grace not only may but ought to be certain; doubt marks weak faith
source_text: XIII. Inde quoque manifestum est fideles qui sunt in Dei gratia, de eo non tantum posse, verum etiam debere certos esse. Et si de eo certi non sint, ac super ea re fluctuent & dubitent, istud in iis arguere defectum & infirmitatem fidei. Nam quum fides vera & viva hujusmodi certitudinem gignat, & ad eam naturali quodam modo tendat, inde consequens est talem certitudinem iis inesse debere, & vitio ipsis ac culpae vertendum si ea destituti illa reperiantur.
pass_a_gloss: From this it is also plain that believers who are in God’s grace not only can but also ought to be certain of it. And if they are not certain of it, and waver and doubt about that matter, that argues in them a defect and weakness of faith. For since true and living faith begets this kind of certainty and tends toward it by a certain natural way, it follows that such certainty ought to be in them, and that it is to be charged to their fault and blame if they are found destitute of it.
pass_b_english: Those in grace ought to be certain of it, not merely able to be.
Wavering about grace signals weak faith, a fault to be amended.

choices.why: Duty of assurance, not mere possibility.
